title: [Workspaces] Migrate Editor from WPF to WinUI 3

proposed_comments.title: Keep executable basenames in consumer lists (1/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep executable basenames in consumer lists (1/2)

**Severity:** `medium`

`TerminateProcessesCA` obtains each executable name with `GetModuleBaseNameW` and compares it literally against this list. The editor's returned name is `PowerToys.WorkspacesEditor.exe`, without the `WinUI3Apps\` directory, so this entry cannot match and this loop skips its editor-specific close/terminate branch. Keep the executable basename here; moving the installed executable does not change its basename. Other shutdown paths may still close the editor, so this is not a claim that installation fails.

```suggestion
        L"PowerToys.WorkspacesEditor.exe",
```

confidence.rationale: Exact upstream API-result/equality mismatch; runner-watcher and other installer shutdown paths explicitly limit the impact claim.

proposed_comments.title: Keep executable basenames in consumer lists (2/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep executable basenames in consumer lists (2/2)

**Severity:** `medium`

`EventViewer::ReportEventViewerInfo` passes each entry as both the query name and the report filename to `EventViewerReporter`. In `EventViewer.cpp`, the reporter appends `"EventViewer-" + fileName + ".xml"` directly to the report directory. This entry therefore produces `EventViewer-WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.WorkspacesEditor.exe.xml`: an unintended nested path whose parent the reporter does not create. When that parent is absent, the report stream cannot open.

Keep the executable basename so the destination is the flat `EventViewer-PowerToys.WorkspacesEditor.exe.xml` report. The registry compatibility consumer in `RegistryUtils.cpp` searches full paths by substring, so the basename still matches an installation under `WinUI3Apps`.

```suggestion
    L"PowerToys.WorkspacesEditor.exe",
```

confidence.rationale: Direct upstream caller/filename trace proves the unintended parent component; registry substring behavior checked. No universal EventData-format or observed event-loss claim.
